claim: The CMP 170HX trains at PCIe x4 because 12 of its 16 lanes ship with their AC-coupling capacitors depopulated; hand-soldering the 24 missing 0402 220 nF X7R capacitors restores a full x16 link with no software patch of any kind.
stance_target: The gap question of whether width beyond x4 needs the AC-coupling capacitor mod — it is the only mechanism, and it is purely mechanical
scope_conditions: CMP 170HX board revisions 180-11001-DAAA-B35 and -B15; 24 parts, two per differential pair across lanes 4-15
quoted_support: the CMP 170HX trains at PCIe x4 because 12 of its 16 lanes ship with their AC-coupling capacitors depopulated from the factory. Hand-soldering 24 missing 0402 220 nF X7R capacitors restores a full x16 link, with no software patch of any kind.

claim: The capacitor mod changes link width only and never PCIe generation: a cap-modded card with no unlocker reports x16 at PCIe 1.0, while an unlocker with no cap mod reports Gen2 x4.
stance_target: The repo's assumption that its fabric is Gen2 x4 — that state is the unlocker-only configuration, not the modded one
scope_conditions: Four-state verification matrix across stock, cap-mod-only, unlocker-only, and both
quoted_support: The capacitor mod changes link width only. It never changes PCIe generation. A cap-modded card with no unlocker installed reports x16 at PCIe 1.0. Conversely, the unlocker without the cap mod reports Gen2 x4.

claim: The four-state verification matrix is: stock LnkSta 'Speed 2.5GT/s, Width x4 (downgraded)' / nvidia-smi 1,1,4; cap mod only 'Speed 2.5GT/s, Width x16' / 1,1,16; unlocker only 'Speed 5GT/s, Width x4 (downgraded)' / 2,2,4; cap mod + unlocker 'Speed 5GT/s, Width x16' / 2,2,16.
stance_target: The repo's pre-flight instruction to record negotiated PCIe width and speed per card
quoted_support: Stock: no mod, no unlocker | Speed 2.5GT/s, Width x4 (downgraded) | 1, 1, 4 ... Capacitor mod + unlocker | Speed 5GT/s, Width x16 | 2, 2, 16

claim: The '(downgraded)' suffix disappearing from the width field once all 24 parts are in place is the single clearest before/after signal, and '(overdriven)' on the speed field is normal rather than an error.
stance_target: How to read the link state correctly after a mod
scope_conditions: lspci LnkSta output after a complete mod with forced Gen2 speed
quoted_support: the (downgraded) suffix disappears from the width field once all 24 parts are in place, which is the single clearest before/after signal. ... (overdriven) on the speed field is normal

claim: Population-to-width mapping: 12 of 24 capacitors correctly populated trains x8; 12-23 of 24 or any bridged/cold joints trains x8; 24 of 24 trains x16 — an x8 result means incomplete solder work, not a hardware limit.
stance_target: How to diagnose a partial mod result
scope_conditions: Multiple modders' progressions x4 -> x8 -> x16 as technique improved
quoted_support: An x8 result after a cap mod means incomplete or bridged solder work, not a distinct hardware limit.

claim: A four-card field report shows all four cap-modded cards training PCIe 2.0 x16 and running continuous four-card LLM inference with zero PCIe errors — the second independent rig to reach Gen2 x16 and the first with more than one card, more than one board revision, and error telemetry.
stance_target: Whether Gen2 x16 is stable enough to plan a training run around, which the PCIe subsystem page had called unestablished
scope_conditions: Four cards, twenty-four Taiyo Yuden MAASJ105SB7224KFCA01 each, photographs and logs supplied; two board revisions
quoted_support: All four train PCIe 2.0 x16 and have run continuous four-card LLM inference with zero PCIe errors. This is the second independent rig to reach Gen2 x16, after the single 2026-07-26 observation, and the first with more than one card, more than one board revision, or any error telemetry at all.

claim: Only the capacitors were fitted for the four-card x16 build: no VBIOS was flashed (all four still report the stock 92.00.6D.00.0A), no VRM phases populated, no strap resistors moved, no backup flash chip added.
stance_target: Whether the mod requires the broader a100-unlock bill of materials — it does not
scope_conditions: Four-card build; circulating a100-unlock.pdf BOM lists a Winbond flash chip and other parts
quoted_support: No VBIOS was flashed: all four cards still report the stock 92.00.6D.00.0A. No VRM phases were populated, no strap resistors were moved, no backup flash chip was added, and no other footprint on the board was touched.

claim: Measured host bandwidth: Gen1 x4 stock ~0.85 GB/s; Gen1 x16 cap-mod-only 2.88 GB/s flat and error-free; Gen2 x4 software-only 1.68 GB/s send / 1.71 GB/s receive; Gen2 x16 both 6.63-6.67 GB/s with nvtop TX 7.061 GiB/s; a second rig 5.97 GB/s host-to-device identical on all four cards.
stance_target: The repo's open question of whether Gen2 x16 would change every communication number ~4x — the measured swing is 1.68-1.71 GB/s to 5.97-6.67 GB/s
scope_conditions: OpenCL-Benchmark / clpeak / ocl_pcie_bw / CUDA H2D with MaxPayload 256 bytes; PCIe 2.0 x16 ceiling is 8 GB/s
quoted_support: Gen2 x16 (both) | 6.63 to 6.67 GB/s | ocl_pcie_bw; nvtop showed TX 7.061 GiB/s at PCIe GEN 2@16x ... Gen2 x16 (both), second rig | 5.97 GB/s host-to-device, identical on all 4 cards

claim: A purely software Gen3 x4 unlock would need no soldering and is the community's next target, but Gen3 x4 is about 3.9 GB/s against Gen2 x16's 8 GB/s, so it lands nearer Gen1 x16 than Gen2 x16.
stance_target: The claim that Gen3 x4 would be speed-equivalent to Gen2 x16
scope_conditions: Arithmetic: Gen3 x4 = 8 GT/s, 128b/130b, four lanes; Gen2 x16 = 8 GB/s
quoted_support: It was described in-channel as speed-equivalent to Gen2 x16, but the arithmetic does not support that: Gen3 x4 is about 3.9 GB/s (8 GT/s, 128b/130b, four lanes) against Gen2 x16's 8 GB/s, so it lands nearer Gen1 x16.

claim: Tensor and expert parallelism were judged unworkable even at PCIe 2.0 x16, and pipeline-parallel inter-card traffic is negligible (10,240 bytes per token per hop for a 5120-hidden model, needing ~25,000 tokens/s to saturate one PCIe 1.0 lane).
stance_target: The repo's claim that EP and TP are ruled out by the fabric while PP remains viable
scope_conditions: Wiki's independent restatement of the parallelism verdict
quoted_support: tensor and expert parallelism were judged unworkable even at PCIe 2.0 x16.

claim: The mod is routine 0402 rework: ~20 minutes per card by hand, fine-point iron at ~380 C, no preheat, no BGA/reball/stencil/firmware step; experienced modders call it 'probably the easiest card to do PCIE mod'.
stance_target: Whether the mod is a realistic option for the box's owner rather than an expert-only procedure
scope_conditions: Labelled, uncramped pads on the back of the board beside the gold fingers
quoted_support: This is routine 0402 rework. ... About 20 minutes per card by hand.

claim: The dominant beginner failure mode is preheating the whole board, whose documented consequence is a bent PCB, broken internal traces and cooked ICs; an imperfect result otherwise under-trains the link rather than damaging the card, with no attempt limit.
stance_target: The risk profile of attempting the mod
scope_conditions: In-channel proposal to preheat in an oven, rejected as a beginner trap; IR stove plus hot air documented as causing damage
quoted_support: The documented real-world consequence of over-preheating (an IR stove plus hot air) is a bent PCB, broken internal traces and cooked ICs ... None of this is destructive. An imperfect result under-trains the link, it does not damage the card

claim: The widely repeated claim that the distributed unlock README documents the x4 limitation as missing AC-coupling capacitors on lanes 4-15 is misattributed: the shipping README.md contains no such text, and neither does any branch or any point in the git history.
stance_target: The provenance of the capacitor-mod explanation in the unlock project's own documentation
scope_conditions: Grep of shipping master, 12 unreleased branches, and full git history
quoted_support: The shipping README.md contains no such text, and neither does any branch or any point in the git history. The technical claim is true and well evidenced; only the attribution to the shipped README is wrong.

claim: The software tree contains nothing about the capacitor mod: no file in shipping master or any of the 12 unreleased branches contains 'capacitor', 'AC coupling', 'solder' or any lane-width register, and the shipping 0007-pcie-gen2.patch manipulates link speed registers only.
stance_target: Whether any software path can widen the link — none exists
scope_conditions: Grep over shipping master, 12 unreleased branches and full git history
quoted_support: No file in shipping master or in any of the 12 unreleased branches contains the strings "capacitor", "AC coupling" or "solder", nor any lane-width register. A grep over the full git history returns nothing.
